sections.markdown:
## C — Knowledge dossier: Occupant protection, load and trip planning

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A26
The handbook’s restraint summary requires appropriate restraints for the driver, front-seat passengers and children under 18 while the vehicle moves. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A26
Small children should ride restrained in the rear rather than in the front passenger seat, especially near an air bag. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A26
A deploying passenger air bag can seriously injure a child seated in front. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A26
The handbook notes that some organizations lend child safety restraints when a family cannot afford one. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A26
The quoted SDCL 32-38-1 rule requires a properly fastened and adjusted belt for a passenger-vehicle driver or front passenger during forward movement on public highways, subject to Chapter 32-37 and Section 32-38-3 exceptions. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A26
The quoted front-seat belt rule concerns the system required when the vehicle was manufactured under federal safety standard 208, cited as 49 C.F.R. 571.208, in effect January 1, 1989. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A26
The quoted rule makes the driver responsible for fastening and adjusting the front-seat belt for a passenger at least 5 but under 18. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A26
A violation of the quoted front-seat belt section is not a moving traffic offense under Section 32-12-49.1. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A26
Air bags supplement seatbelts and work best with them, so belts must still be worn in an air-bag-equipped vehicle. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A26
Seatbelts help position the body for air-bag protection and restrain occupants during the initial crash and later impacts. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A26
Consult the vehicle owner’s manual for the air bags installed in that vehicle. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A26
A child seat must be installed and used correctly according to the applicable equipment instructions. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A26
Children aged 12 or younger should be restrained in the rear seat, and a rear-facing child seat must never be placed ahead of an active passenger air bag. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A26
The handbook describes an infant carrier as a reclining rear-facing seat with impact cushioning, attached to the vehicle by the lap belt while its built-in harness holds the baby. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A27
A household baby seat is not a vehicle-protective infant carrier and should not be used as one. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A27
The printed carrier paragraph says to use it from birth until the child sits well alone, described as around 9 months, and says many models can convert to an upright forward-facing toddler seat. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A27
Holding a child in an adult’s arms is unsafe during a crash even when the adult is belted. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A27
Never place a seatbelt around both an adult and a child sitting on the adult’s lap. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A27
Use an approved child restraint starting with the baby’s first ride home from the hospital. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A27
The handbook generally favors the rear seat over the front and the center over the sides for children, while warning against a driver repeatedly turning around to check on them. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A27
An unrestrained passenger can injure other occupants who are wearing belts. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A27
Under the quoted Section 32-37-1, a passenger-vehicle driver on South Dakota streets or highways must secure a child under 5 in a child restraint according to its manufacturer’s instructions. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A27
That child-restraint excerpt identifies federal safety standard 213 as it stood on January 1, 1981. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A27
The quoted child-restraint law says a child under 5 who weighs at least 40 pounds may satisfy that section by using a seatbelt. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A27
Violating the quoted under-five child-restraint section is classified as a petty offense. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A27
The quoted Section 32-37-1.2 requires a driver aged at least 14 but under 18 to wear an adjusted and fastened safety belt while a passenger vehicle moves on a public street or highway. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A27
The minor-driver belt excerpt applies to the belt required under federal standard 208, 49 C.F.R. 571.208, in effect January 1, 1989, and classifies a violation as a petty offense. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A27
The quoted Sections 32-37-1 through 32-37-1.3 do not apply to passenger cars built before 1966 that have not been fitted with seatbelts. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A27
The quoted restraint chapter says noncompliance is neither contributory or comparative negligence nor assumption of risk and cannot be evidence in a civil trial. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0027]

Misconceptions: An adult’s arms do not replace a child restraint, a shared adult-child belt is unsafe, and short local trips do not justify skipping a belt.
Mnemonics: Use person, position, restraint and load as an authored preparation cue.
Glossary: Air bags are supplemental restraints; a child carrier is vehicle protection rather than a household baby seat; a secure load cannot shift into the road or air.
Dynamic facts: The dated carrier and seat-guide entries require current primary-source verification before learner release; equipment must follow its applicable manufacturer instructions.
